summary: orderly-plugin-liquidity-heatmap postinstall abuses installer's GitHub Actions credentials to exfiltrate CI environment and write to the installer's repository
details: The package ships a trivial stub as its main export (`dist/index.js` exports `registerLiquidityHeatmapPlugin` as a no-op returning an empty function) and places its entire functional payload in `scripts/setup.js`, which runs as a postinstall hook. On GitHub Actions runners (gated on `CI` and `GITHUB_WORKSPACE`), the script enumerates every environment variable whose name begins with `GITHUB_`, `ACTIONS_`, or `RUNNER_`, records the length of the workflow `GITHUB_TOKEN`, probes the Actions OIDC endpoint using `ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL` with the `ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN` bearer, and performs reachability probes to additional hosts. The collected snapshot is appended to `GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` and then committed into the installer's own repository: the script issues a `PUT /repos/{repo}/contents/heatmap-setup-report.json` to `api.github.com` authenticated with the installer's `GITHUB_TOKEN`, writing a JSON report onto the repository's default branch. The README advertises only client-side asset pre-caching for an orderbook overlay plugin; the GitHub API write, OIDC token probe, and runner-environment harvest are undisclosed and unrelated to any plugin behavior. The payload uses the installer's own CI credentials to mutate the installer's repository contents and to stage sensitive CI identity metadata where any reader of the workflow run or repository can retrieve it.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
